Definition: neuter of the comparative of the same as G196; (adverbially) more exactly:--more perfect(-ly).
BiblicalUsage: Three times, always of knowing or explaining more exactly. Priscilla and Aquila take Apollos aside and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly; the Jews ask the chief captain to bring Paul down as though ye would enquire something more perfectly concerning him; and Felix, having more perfect knowledge of that way, defers Paul's case.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for more exactly carries little weight on its own; its weight is the scene, two friends taking a gifted preacher aside to teach him more perfectly, and his gladness to learn.
RelatedEvents: Apollos Taught at Ephesus; Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
